subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — Latency & Throughput follow-up (PayZ)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: John Stevens <john@payz.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated (latency/throughput recap)

Hi John — great to meet you and the PayZ team today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we promised to follow up on:  

- Business need: real-time fraud-screening for payments (decision path).  
- Traffic profile: peak ~500 requests/sec (concurrent inference calls), average 150–200 rps.  
- Per-request model payload: ~350 tokens in, ~150 tokens out; estimate ~100M tokens/day at current forecast.  
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <150ms for the model call (application-level SLO).  
- Compliance/segmentation: data segregation desired; HIPAA not required at this stage but may need strict access controls.  

Initial guidance: from a throughput/latency standpoint, Dedicated capacity is the safer choice if you need consistent p95 latency at 500 rps and want predictable cost and isolation. Hosted API can often meet the targets for bursty or lower sustained loads, especially with caching and smaller model choices, but it does not provide the same reserved throughput guarantees or private network options.  

Attachments: I attached a preliminary Dedicated capacity estimate and our latest performance benchmarks for the 8k-context model we discussed. Please review — I called out two capacity bands (baseline and 2x for safety).

Next steps:  
1) Can you confirm the true peak concurrent calls during batch windows (are there scheduled peaks at midnight/EOY)?  
2) Would the procurement team want a sample SOW or a short POC (2-week) to validate latency under your traffic?  
3) If helpful, we can schedule a short runbook review with Rishi (SE) to map instance sizing to your exact request mix.  

Thanks — I’ll coordinate availability for a 30-min PoC kickoff if you’re ready.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Thanks Neha — quick clarifications:  
- The 500 rps is our absolute peak during settlement windows (~5 minutes, twice per night). Outside those windows we're typically 80–120 rps.  
- End-to-end p95 target is 150ms but we can tolerate occasional spikes during non-peak hours.  
- Isolation: we prefer a ded. pool or VPC peering for security and auditability. Not full HIPAA yet, but could be required later.  

POC sounds good — procurement will want a short doc outlining expected costs if we run a 2-week dedicated pilot. Can Rishi share a simple test harness we can run against our traffic generator?

-John

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: John Stevens <john@payz.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated (latency/throughput recap)

Hi John — Rishi from SE here. Quick technical notes based on Neha's summary + your clarifications:  

1) Latency math: for the model we discussed (8k context, ~350 in / 150 out) our internal benchmarks show per-request model time of ~40–60ms on a dedicated instance with optimized kernels, plus ~20–40ms for network/serialization at your scale. That stacks up to a typical p95 around 100–140ms on Dedicated with correct instance sizing and batching disabled for low-latency paths.  

2) Hosted API caveats: hosted endpoints can meet p95 <200ms for moderate sustained loads, but p95 can vary more due to multi-tenant noisy neighbors and routing. We do offer priority routing but it is not equivalent to reserved capacity.  

3) Throughput: 500 rps sustained is better served by Dedicated pools. Our capacity estimate (attached) shows a baseline of 6 x A100-ish instances to comfortably hit 500 rps with headroom. If you prefer lower cost we can explore mixed model and quantized variants; that changes latency by ~10–20ms in our tests.  

4) Test harness: attaching a simple load script and a set of example prompts. We can run a small PoC where PayZ drives traffic into a dedicated pool in our staging and we capture p50/p95/p99.

Proposed next steps:  
- If PayZ signs a 2-week PoC (SOW attached as draft), we will spin up the Dedicated pool and provide the harness + a runbook.  
- Post-POC we transition to either Reserved commit or a hybrid Hosted+Dedic model depending on cost/latency tradeoffs you observe.

I'll be on the kickoff call and can own the benching.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: performance-benchmarks-8k.pdf (pdf), sow-payz-draft.docx (docx)
